nodes.summary: For every Boolean value $b$, its sign $\sigma(b)$, which is $1$ for true and $-1$ for false, satisfies $|\sigma(b)| = 1$.
nodes.title: Coordinate signs have absolute value one

nodes.summary: For all real-valued functions $f$ and $g$ on the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates and every set $S$ of the $n$ coordinates, the Fourier coefficient of $f + g$ at $S$ is the sum of the Fourier coefficients of $f$ and $g$ at $S$: $\widehat{f + g}(S) = \hat f(S) + \hat g(S)$.
nodes.title: Additivity of Fourier coefficients

nodes.summary: For every real $\rho$, every real-valued function $f$ on the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates and every set $S$ of the $n$ coordinates, the Fourier coefficient at $S$ of $T_\rho f$, the noise operator with parameter $\rho$ applied to $f$, is $\widehat{T_\rho f}(S) = \rho^{|S|} \hat f(S)$.
nodes.title: Fourier coefficients of the noise operator

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a real-valued function on the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates, let $i$ be a coordinate, and let $g(x) = f(x^{\oplus i})$, where $x^{\oplus i}$ is the point $x$ with its $i$-th coordinate flipped. Write $\hat f(S)$ and $\hat g(S)$ for the Fourier coefficients of $f$ and $g$ at a set $S$ of the $n$ coordinates. Then for every such $S$, $\hat g(S) = -\hat f(S)$ if $i \in S$ and $\hat g(S) = \hat f(S)$ if…
nodes.title: Flipping a coordinate negates the Fourier coefficients of the sets containing it

nodes.summary: For every real $c$, every real-valued function $f$ on the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates and every set $S$ of the $n$ coordinates, the Fourier coefficient of $c f$ at $S$ is $c$ times the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$: $\widehat{c f}(S) = c \hat f(S)$.
nodes.title: Homogeneity of Fourier coefficients

nodes.summary: For every real $c$ and every set $S$ of the $n$ coordinates, the Fourier coefficient at $S$ of the constant function $x \mapsto c$ on the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates is $c$ if $S = \emptyset$ and $0$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Fourier coefficients of a constant function

nodes.summary: For all sets $S$ and $T$ of the $n$ coordinates, the Fourier coefficient at $S$ of the Fourier character $\chi_T$ on the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates, $\chi_T(x) = \prod_{i \in T} \sigma(x_i)$ with $\sigma(\text{true}) = 1$ and $\sigma(\text{false}) = -1$, is $1$ if $T = S$ and $0$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Fourier coefficients of a character

nodes.summary: For every real-valued function $f$ on the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates and every set $S$ of the $n$ coordinates, the Fourier coefficient $\hat f(S)$ is the average of $f(x) \chi_S(x)$ over all points $x$ of the cube, $\hat f(S) = \mathbb{E}_x [f(x) \chi_S(x)]$, where $\chi_S$ is the Fourier character of $S$.
nodes.title: Fourier coefficients as averages

nodes.summary: For every real-valued function $f$ on the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates and every set $S$ of the $n$ coordinates, the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$ is $\hat f(S) = \frac{1}{2^n} \sum_x f(x) \chi_S(x)$, where the sum runs over all points $x$ of the cube and $\chi_S$ is the Fourier character of $S$.
nodes.title: Fourier coefficients as sums over the cube

nodes.summary: If two real-valued functions $f$ and $g$ on the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates have the same Fourier coefficient $\hat f(S) = \hat g(S)$ at every set $S$ of the $n$ coordinates, then $f = g$.
nodes.title: Fourier coefficients determine the function

nodes.summary: For real-valued functions $f$ and $g$ on the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ and every set $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the Fourier coefficient of $f - g$ at $S$ is $\widehat{f - g}(S) = \hat f(S) - \hat g(S)$.
nodes.title: Fourier coefficients of a difference

nodes.summary: For real numbers $a_T$ indexed by the sets $T \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, let $g(x) = \sum_T a_T \chi_T(x)$ on the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$, where $\chi_T$ is the Fourier character of $T$. Then for every set $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ the Fourier coefficient of $g$ at $S$ is $\hat g(S) = a_S$.
nodes.title: Uniqueness of the Fourier expansion

nodes.summary: For every real number $c$ and every coordinate $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the influence of coordinate $i$ on the constant function with value $c$ on the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ is $0$.
nodes.title: Constant functions have zero influence

nodes.summary: Let $f$ be a real-valued function on the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ that takes only the values $1$ and $-1$, and let $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$. Then the influence of coordinate $i$ on $f$ equals the probability, for $x$ uniform on the cube, that $f(x^{\oplus i}) \ne f(x)$, where $x^{\oplus i}$ is $x$ with its $i$-th coordinate flipped.
nodes.title: Influence of a Boolean function as a flip probability

nodes.summary: For every real-valued function $f$ on the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ and every coordinate $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the influence of coordinate $i$ on $f$ is $\mathrm{Inf}_i[f] = \sum_{S \ni i} \hat f(S)^2$, where $\hat f(S)$ is the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$ and the sum runs over the sets $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ that contain $i$.
nodes.title: Fourier formula for influence

nodes.summary: For every real-valued function $f$ on the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ and every coordinate $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the influence $\mathrm{Inf}_i[f]$ of coordinate $i$ on $f$ satisfies $\mathrm{Inf}_i[f] \ge 0$.
nodes.title: Influences are nonnegative

nodes.summary: For a real-valued function $f$ on the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ and a coordinate $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the influence of $i$ on $f$ is $\mathrm{Inf}_i[f] = \mathbb{E}_x\big[\big((f(x) - f(x^{\oplus i})) / 2\big)^2\big]$, where the expectation is over $x$ uniform on the cube and $x^{\oplus i}$ is $x$ with its $i$-th coordinate flipped.
nodes.title: Influence of a coordinate

nodes.summary: For all real numbers $\rho$ and $\sigma$ and every real-valued function $f$ on the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$, applying the noise operator $T_\sigma$ and then $T_\rho$ to $f$ gives $T_{\rho\sigma} f$: $T_\rho(T_\sigma f) = T_{\rho\sigma} f$.
nodes.title: Semigroup property of the noise operator

nodes.summary: For every real number $\rho$ and every real number $c$, the noise operator $T_\rho$ maps the constant function with value $c$ on the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ to itself.
nodes.title: The noise operator fixes constants

nodes.summary: For every real number $\rho$ and every set $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the noise operator $T_\rho$ maps the Fourier character $\chi_S$ on the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ to the function $x \mapsto \rho^{|S|} \chi_S(x)$, so $\chi_S$ is an eigenfunction of $T_\rho$ with eigenvalue $\rho^{|S|}$.
nodes.title: Characters are eigenfunctions of the noise operator

nodes.summary: For every real number $\rho$, every function $f$ from the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ to $\mathbb{R}$ and every point $x$ of the cube,
nodes.title: Fourier expansion of the noise operator

nodes.summary: For every real number $\rho$ with $|\rho| \le 1$, the noise operator $T_\rho$ on the Boolean cube maps nonnegative functions to nonnegative functions: if $f$ is a real function on the cube with $f(y) \ge 0$ for every point $y$, then $T_\rho f(x) \ge 0$ for every point $x$ of the cube.
nodes.title: Positivity of the noise operator

nodes.summary: For every function $f$ from the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ to $\mathbb{R}$, the noise operator with $\rho = 1$ fixes $f$: $T_1 f = f$.
nodes.title: The noise operator $T_1$ is the identity

nodes.summary: For every function $f$ from the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ to $\mathbb{R}$, the noise operator with $\rho = 0$ sends $f$ to the constant function whose value is the mean $\mathbb{E}_x f(x) = 2^{-n} \sum_x f(x)$ of $f$ under the uniform distribution.
nodes.title: The noise operator $T_0$ takes the mean

nodes.summary: For a real number $\rho$ and a function $f$ from the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ to $\mathbb{R}$, the noise operator $T_\rho$ sends $f$ to the function
nodes.title: Noise operator on the Boolean cube

nodes.summary: For every real number $c$, the constant function with value $c$ on the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ has total influence $0$.
nodes.title: Constant functions have zero total influence

nodes.summary: For every function $f$ from the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ to $\mathbb{R}$, the total influence of $f$ is
nodes.title: Total influence in Fourier form

nodes.summary: For every function $f$ from the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ to $\mathbb{R}$, the total influence of $f$ is nonnegative.
nodes.title: Total influence is nonnegative

nodes.summary: For a function $f$ from the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ to $\mathbb{R}$, the total influence of $f$ is the sum of the influences of its $n$ coordinates, $\mathrm{I}[f] = \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} \mathrm{Inf}_i[f]$, where $\mathrm{Inf}_i[f] = \mathbb{E}_x \left[\left(\frac{f(x) - f(x^{\oplus i})}{2}\right)^2\right]$, $x^{\oplus i}$ is $x$ with its $i$-th coordinate flipped and $\mathbb{E}_x$ is the uniform average over the…
nodes.title: Total influence on the Boolean cube

nodes.summary: For every real number $c$, the constant function with value $c$ on the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ has variance $0$ under the uniform distribution.
nodes.title: Constant functions have zero variance

nodes.summary: For every function $f : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ on the Boolean cube, the variance of $f$ under the uniform distribution equals $\mathbb{E}_x[f(x)^2] - (\mathbb{E}_x[f(x)])^2$, where $\mathbb{E}_x$ denotes the uniform average over the $2^n$ points $x$ of the cube.
nodes.title: Variance as mean square minus squared mean

nodes.summary: For every function $f : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ on the Boolean cube, the variance of $f$ under the uniform distribution equals $\sum_{S \neq \emptyset} \hat f(S)^2$, where the sum runs over the nonempty sets $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and $\hat f(S)$ is the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$.
nodes.title: Variance in terms of Fourier coefficients

nodes.summary: For every function $f : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ on the Boolean cube, the variance of $f$ under the uniform distribution is at most the total influence of $f$: $\mathrm{Var}[f] \le I[f]$.
nodes.title: Poincaré inequality on the Boolean cube

nodes.summary: For every function $f : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ on the Boolean cube, the variance of $f$ under the uniform distribution is at least $0$.
nodes.title: Variance on the Boolean cube is nonnegative

nodes.summary: For a function $f : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ on the Boolean cube, its variance under the uniform distribution is $\mathrm{Var}[f] = \mathbb{E}_x\big[(f(x) - \mathbb{E}_y[f(y)])^2\big]$, where $\mathbb{E}_x$ denotes the uniform average over the $2^n$ points $x$ of the cube.
nodes.title: Variance on the Boolean cube

nodes.summary: Let $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, let $x$ be a point of the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates, let $i < n$, and write $x^{\oplus i}$ for $x$ with coordinate $i$ flipped. Then the Fourier character $\chi_S$ satisfies $\chi_S(x^{\oplus i}) = -\chi_S(x)$ if $i \in S$, and $\chi_S(x^{\oplus i}) = \chi_S(x)$ if $i \notin S$.
nodes.title: Flipping a coordinate in a Fourier character

nodes.summary: For every Boolean value $b$, its sign $\sigma(b)$ (equal to $1$ for true and $-1$ for false) is nonzero.
nodes.title: Coordinate signs are nonzero

nodes.summary: For every Boolean value $b$, the sign of its negation is the negative of its sign: $\sigma(\lnot b) = -\sigma(b)$, where $\sigma(\text{true}) = 1$ and $\sigma(\text{false}) = -1$.
nodes.title: Sign of a negated Boolean value

nodes.summary: For every real $\rho$ and every function $f : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ on the Boolean cube, the uniform average over the cube of $T_\rho f$, the image of $f$ under the noise operator with parameter $\rho$, equals the uniform average of $f$.
nodes.title: The noise operator preserves the mean

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid that is a module over the nonnegative rationals, let $f$ be a function from the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates to $M$, and let $i < n$. Writing $x^{\oplus i}$ for $x$ with coordinate $i$ flipped, the uniform average of $f(x^{\oplus i})$ over all points $x$ of the cube equals the uniform average of $f(x)$.
nodes.title: Averages are invariant under flipping a coordinate

nodes.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every function $f : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$, the uniform average $\mathbb{E}_x f(x)$ of $f$ over the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ equals the Fourier coefficient $\hat f(\emptyset)$ of $f$ at the empty set.
nodes.title: Average over the Boolean cube as the empty Fourier coefficient

nodes.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every function $f : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$, the uniform average of $f$ over the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ is $\mathbb{E}_x f(x) = \frac{1}{2^n} \sum_{x \in \{-1, 1\}^n} f(x)$.
nodes.title: Uniform average over the Boolean cube as a sum

nodes.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and all functions $f, g : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$, the uniform average of $f g$ over the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ is the sum, over all sets $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, of the products of the Fourier coefficients of $f$ and $g$ at $S$: $\mathbb{E}_x f(x) g(x) = \sum_S \hat f(S) \hat g(S)$.
nodes.title: Plancherel's identity on the Boolean cube

nodes.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every function $f : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$, the uniform average of $f^2$ over the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ is the sum, over all sets $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, of the squares of the Fourier coefficients of $f$ at $S$: $\mathbb{E}_x f(x)^2 = \sum_S \hat f(S)^2$.
nodes.title: Parseval's identity on the Boolean cube

nodes.summary: For every point $x$ of the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ and all coordinates $i, j \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ with $j \ne i$, the $j$-th coordinate of $x^{\oplus i}$, the point $x$ with its $i$-th coordinate flipped, is $x_j$.
nodes.title: A coordinate flip fixes the other coordinates

nodes.summary: For every point $x$ of the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ and every coordinate $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the $i$-th coordinate of $x^{\oplus i}$, the point $x$ with its $i$-th coordinate flipped, is the negation $\lnot x_i$ of $x_i$ (true and false exchanged).
nodes.title: A coordinate flip negates the flipped coordinate

nodes.summary: For every point $x$ of the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ and every coordinate $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, writing $x^{\oplus i}$ for $x$ with its $i$-th coordinate flipped, we have $(x^{\oplus i})^{\oplus i} = x$.
nodes.title: Flipping a coordinate twice

nodes.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every coordinate $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the map $x \mapsto x^{\oplus i}$ on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$, which flips the $i$-th coordinate, is an involution: applying it twice gives the identity.
nodes.title: Flipping a coordinate is an involution

nodes.summary: For every point $x$ of the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ and every coordinate $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the point $x^{\oplus i}$ obtained from $x$ by flipping its $i$-th coordinate is different from $x$.
nodes.title: A coordinate flip moves every point

nodes.summary: For a point $x$ of the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ and a coordinate $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the point $x^{\oplus i}$ is obtained from $x$ by negating its $i$-th coordinate (exchanging true and false) and leaving every other coordinate unchanged.
nodes.title: Coordinate flip on the Boolean cube

nodes.summary: Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$, and let $x$ be a point of the cube. For each subset $S$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ let $\hat f(S)$ be the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$ and $\chi_S$ the Fourier character of $S$. Then $\sum_S \hat f(S) \chi_S(x) = f(x)$, the sum ranging over all subsets $S$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$.
nodes.title: Fourier inversion on the Boolean cube

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be an additive commutative monoid, $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $f$ a function from the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ to $M$, and $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$. For a point $x$ of the cube write $x^{\oplus i}$ for the point $x$ with its $i$-th coordinate flipped. Then $\sum_x f(x^{\oplus i}) = \sum_x f(x)$, both sums ranging over all points $x$ of the cube.
nodes.title: Flipping a coordinate preserves sums over the cube

nodes.summary: Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and let $x, y$ be points of the Boolean cube of dimension $n$. For each subset $S$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ let $\chi_S$ be the Fourier character of $S$. Then $\sum_S \chi_S(x) \chi_S(y)$, the sum ranging over all subsets $S$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, equals $2^n$ if $x = y$ and $0$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Dual orthogonality of the Boolean cube characters

nodes.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every subset $S$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the sum of the Fourier character $\chi_S$ over all points of the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ equals $2^n$ if $S$ is empty and $0$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Sum of a Boolean cube character

nodes.summary: Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$, let $S$ and $T$ be subsets of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, and let $\chi_S$ and $\chi_T$ be their Fourier characters. Then $\sum_x \chi_S(x) \chi_T(x)$, the sum ranging over all points $x$ of the Boolean cube of dimension $n$, equals $2^n$ if $S = T$ and $0$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Orthogonality of the Boolean cube characters
